name: Little Falls rapid water filtration
description: East Jersey Water Company built a rapid filtration installation at Little Falls, New Jersey.

date.basis: Year reported for this scoped historical event; not a universal invention date.

events.statement: The East Jersey Water Company built a filtration installation at Little Falls, New Jersey.

evidence.supports: Dates the East Jersey installation to 1902 and describes the concrete filters.
Attributes the filter to the East Jersey Water Company.

events.caveats: The source says built in 1902; the start of full service is not independently dated by this passage.

date.basis: Year reported for this scoped historical event; not a universal invention date.

events.statement: Municipal engineers inspected the plant, whose contemporary description reported 32 filters and their nominal capacity.

evidence.locator: Printed p. 192, inspection heading and plant description
evidence.supports: Dates the 1904 inspection and gives the number and nominal capacity of filters.

events.caveats: Nominal design capacity is not actual daily output or a count of people supplied.

earliest_record.rationale: Earliest supported event for this scoped case, not a worldwide priority claim.

caveats: The later historical account dates construction to 1902; another EPA history says 1901. Treat the 1902 date as reported, not a resolution of that discrepancy or a global first.

research.note: Independent review checked the HAER construction account and the municipal engineers’ plant description on printed p. 192. The publisher-indexed text includes the 11 June 1904 inspection heading omitted by one PDF text extraction. Capacity remains nominal, and the conflicting 1901/1902 construction chronology remains unresolved.

measures.quantity: filter count reported in plant description
measures.subject: Little Falls plant at the 1904 inspection

measures.quantity: nominal daily capacity of each filter
